evidence.field: 形義源流通解; 甲骨、金文、說文、廣韻
evidence.text: The database reports 后 in bronze inscriptions from the late Spring and Autumn period, with the sense 'ruler'. It says bronze forms distinguish right-facing 后 from left-facing 司, while oracle forms do not distinguish orientation; it attributes to Tang Lan and Li Xiaoding the view that 后 and 司 were originally the same graph. It separately reports Wang Guowei's identification of oracle 后 written with 毓. The database reproduces the Shuowen account ('successor ruler', human figure, issuing commands) as an early lexicographic interpretation, and records the Guangyun fanqie 胡口 and 胡遘. This supports competing paleographic accounts, not a settled decomposition of modern 后 into 𠂆 plus 口.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：后

evidence.source: 教育部《異體字字典》 (Taiwan Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants)
evidence.text: Lists 'ruler' as a sense of 后 and quotes Shuowen's 繼體君也; also cites Shijing 商頌·玄鳥 and Zuozhuan 僖公三十二年 examples in royal contexts. It gives later senses including feudal lord and ruler's principal wife, with a Guangyun gloss 皇后也 and a Han shu 景帝紀 usage. These are separately cited historical senses; they do not establish that the original graph depicted childbirth or a rear body part.
evidence.title: [A00511] 后 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.field: 甲骨、金文、戰國簡帛、說文、形義源流通解
evidence.text: The database proposes oracle graph 幺 + 夂 as the early form of 後: 夂 is interpreted as a foot and 幺 as a restraining cord, yielding the idea of lagging; 彳 was added later as a walking indicator. It explicitly records an alternative analysis in which 幺 is phonetic (attributed to Liu Zhao and He Linyi), so its semantic/phonetic role is disputed. It cites an oracle-bone usage in 屯南2358, 後王射兕, for succession/order; bronze examples for lagging, temporal after, descendants, and an asserted sense 'end'; and Warring States bamboo texts for descendants/successor. Bronze and bamboo forms sometimes use 辵 in place of 彳, consistent with Shuowen's separate old form 𨒥. The item treats this as a graphic and lexical history of 後, distinct from 后.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：後

evidence.text: For 後, the database reproduces Shuowen's 遲也 and its analysis 从彳、幺、夊, plus a separate ancient form 𨒥 从辵. Guangyun lists 胡口 and 胡遘, matching the two listed tone categories. This is evidence for the historical dictionary tradition and readings, not proof that the Shuowen graph analysis is correct.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：後

evidence.field: 普通話; 中古音; 繁簡對應
evidence.text: Both 后 and 後 are listed with Mandarin hòu. Both pages give Guangyun fanqie 胡口 (upper tone) and 胡遘 (departing tone), with Middle Chinese categories 匣母, 侯韻, first division. The database displays 后 and 後 as a traditional/simplified mapping, documenting current graphic merger in simplified Chinese, not an ancient phonetic-compound relationship.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：后

evidence.source: 教育部《異體字字典》 (Taiwan Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants)
evidence.field: 后 sense 3; citations to Guangyun and Han shu
evidence.text: The dictionary distinguishes the royal-ruler sense of 后 from the 'ruler's principal wife' sense, citing Guangyun's 皇后也 and a Han shu 景帝紀 passage. This supports a documented lexical development to 'empress/queen' in received textual usage; the source does not date the semantic transition or demonstrate a childbirth-to-succession chain.
evidence.title: [A00511] 后 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.text: The source asserts that orientation distinctions for 后 and 司 appear only in bronze forms and that oracle graphs are directionally indistinct; it attributes the same-graph analysis to named scholars. Thus describing 司 merely as a 'mirror image' of 后 risks projecting a later distinction back onto oracle script. No component-by-component derivation or corruption process is demonstrated in the inspected text.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：后

evidence.field: modern and historical readings for 後
evidence.text: The page provides modern Mandarin hòu and historical Guangyun fanqie 胡口 / 胡遘, mapped to Middle Chinese 匣母侯韻, upper and departing tones. It does not provide a reconstruction for 幺 on this page, and the disputed sound-component proposal is attributed to scholars without historical readings there. Therefore a same-system reconstructed pronunciation comparison for 幺 and 後 remains unverified in this research.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：後

search_audit.outcome: Search found a ministry dictionary result snippet stating classical borrowing of 后 for 後 and modern simplified-character consolidation. The direct ministry page failed to fetch (cache miss); a research PDF failed to open because its content was too large; the Ministry of Education page hit a redirect loop. gaps: The origin of 后 remains unsettled in the inspected evidence: the source reports same-graph/orientation analysis for 后 and 司, and separately reports oracle 后 written with 毓, but no visually inspected glyph evidence or decisive component analysis was available.

The source reports late Spring and Autumn bronze attestation for 后 as a ruler but does not give a secure date for the earliest oracle-bone uses or settle whether those oracle uses were the same lexeme and graph later distinguished as 后.

The proposed childbirth → succession → empress semantic chain is attributed in the dossier to Wang Guowei but is not established by the inspected source text as a dated sequence. The proposed anus/rear-body analysis is likewise unsupported by inspected paleographic evidence.

The 後 analysis 幺 + 夂 as cord plus foot is explicitly disputed by a sound-component account for 幺. I found no inspected independent reconstruction of 幺 in the same system as 後, so the phonetic proposal cannot be evaluated here from a pronunciation match.

Earliest separate attestation for 後 senses beyond the database's cited oracle usage was not independently checked against primary inscription editions; the database supplies vessel/text identifiers but not dates for each inscription.

A ministry dictionary search result reports that 后 was used in transmitted texts as a loan for 後 and that modern simplified standards made 后 a simplified form of 後. The target result page could not be opened, so details and dates for the classical loan and standardization remain unverified here.

The accessed pages give modern Mandarin hòu and Middle Chinese fanqie for 后 and 後, but not an inspected Old Chinese reconstruction system comparison for both entries; dossier reconstructions from different named systems should not be treated as interchangeable without checking their original sources.

No evidence was found in the inspected material establishing a Proto-Sino-Tibetan cognate as part of the graph's formation; that lexical-comparative claim is outside what these graph-history sources establish.

A direct ctext Shuowen page attempt returned an internal error. The Shuowen wording was inspected through the CUHK dictionary's reproduced entry, not through an independently opened primary text page.
